```{python}
#| include: false
from cohort_common import *
from clinical import dense_share, rule_groups

usable_results = rule_results(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)
higher, compared, _ = usable_results["CANCER vs NORMAL"]
interval = binomtest(higher, compared).proportion_ci(method="exact")
found = rule_breasts(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)
both = sorted({n for n, _ in found if (n, "LEFT") in found and (n, "RIGHT") in found})
normal_pairs = sum(found[n, "LEFT"][0] == found[n, "RIGHT"][0] == "NORMAL" for n in both)
young_cancer = sum(label == "CANCER" and nova_age.get(nova, np.inf) < 40 for nova, side, label in breast_use)
THRESHOLDS = (0.25, 0.35, 0.45, 0.55)
by_threshold = {t: rule_results(t, CENTRE_MIN)["CANCER vs NORMAL"] for t in THRESHOLDS}
threshold_text = ", ".join(f"{h / n:.0%} at {t:g} ({h}/{n})" for t, (h, n, _) in by_threshold.items())
```

::: {.callout-warning title="What limits these results"}
1. **Small numbers.** The headline rests on `{python} compared` CANCER/NORMAL patients: `{python} f"{higher / compared:.0%}"`, with a 95%
   confidence interval of `{python} f"{interval.low:.0%}–{interval.high:.0%}"`. It is a pilot result.
2. **Only CANCER vs NORMAL is supported on the threshold rule.** The wettest 15% of samples separate NORMAL < BENIGN < CANCER (@fig-top15), but
   under the fixed usable-scan cut of @sec-the-rule BENIGN and CANCER look almost the same, and the paired test for BENIGN vs NORMAL is
   `{python} rule_text(usable_results, "BENIGN vs NORMAL")` and for CANCER vs BENIGN `{python} rule_text(usable_results, "CANCER vs BENIGN")`,
   neither above chance. Distinguishing benign from cancer is what clinicians need most, and this analysis does not yet do it. **Mapping would
   address this:** a whole-breast map lets us keep the wettest tissue in each breast (the top-15% idea of @sec-water-rich) and compare that,
   instead of a few single points that only just clear a fixed threshold (@sec-mapping).
3. **Few young CANCER breasts.** Only `{python} young_cancer` CANCER breasts under 40 have a usable scan, so nothing can be said about that age group
   (@sec-usable-and-rejected-scans-by-age).
4. **A thin healthy baseline.** Only `{python} normal_pairs` NORMAL/NORMAL patients have usable scans in both breasts, so how different two healthy
   breasts are is barely measured (@sec-glandular-details).
5. **The rule selects dense breasts.** BI-RADS C/D (dense) make up `{python} f"{dense_share['compared']:.0%}"` of the patients compared against
   `{python} f"{dense_share['left out']:.0%}"` of those left out (@fig-who-left-out). The result applies to dense breasts; for fattier breasts it
   currently says nothing.
6. **The threshold sits at a peak.** The CANCER vs NORMAL share is `{python} threshold_text`. The chosen `{python} f"{WATER_MIN:g}"` is at a
   peak of this curve (@fig-on-the-fly), so the `{python} f"{higher / compared:.0%}"` is likely the optimistic end, and it was chosen on the same
   patients it is reported on. The result stays above chance at every threshold. **Mapping would address this:** selection becomes a percentile
   within each breast after the scan, not a global threshold tuned on this cohort (@sec-mapping).
:::
